As per office report, there is a delay of 239 days in preferring this Government Appeal as well as leave to appeal application.
Since, we have satisfied with the reasons, so furnished, which occasioned in delay condonation application
, therefore, delay of 239 days is condoned.
Delay condonation application (IA/1/2024) made therefor, is allowed.
Special Leave to Appeal No.420 of 2024 2.

The State has preferred this application seeking leave to appeal against judgment and order dated 26.10.2023 passed by learned Fourth Additional Sessions Judge, Haridwar in Sessions Trial No.221 of 2022 State Vs. Manish, whereby, the said Court, at the end of trial, has acquitted the respondent- accused for the charges punishable under Sections 328/34, 379/34 and 413/34 IPC.

sentences.text: The facts of the case in nutshell are that the informant along with his family had come to Haridwar on 18.11.2021 by his Creta Car.
He had to return to Delhi on 20.11.2021.

In the morning of 20.11.2021, his driver named- Harish Yadav was administered some intoxicated substance, which State Of Uttarakhand -- Applicant/ vs Manish on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85244638/

sentences.text: With these averments, the report was lodged.
4. The matter was investigated.
The case was registered against the unknown persons under Sections 379 and 328 IPC.
The Investigating Officer, on completion of investigation, submitted a charge-sheet against the present accused Manish under Sections 328, 34, 379 and 413 IPC in the Court.
Charges were accordingly framed against the respondent-accused, which he denied and claimed for trial.

5. The prosecution examined as many as three witnesses, namely, PW-1 Aadarsh Kumar (informant), PW-2 Harish Kumar and PW-3 Sub Inspector Anshul Agrawal, before the learned trial court to prove its case against the respondent/accused and documentary evidences were also produced.

Thereafter, the statement of respondent/accused was recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C.,
in which, he stated that he has been falsely implicated with the aforesaid crime by the prosecution.
6. Learned trial court at the end of trial does not find favour with the prosecution story, and, it accordingly acquitted the respondent-accused, as mentioned in Para 2 of this judgment.

Hence,
challenging the findings of acquittal, State 2024:UHC:7485-DB has come up with this appeal before this Court along with application seeking leave to appeal.
7. The charge against the accused is of Section 328, 379 and 413 IPC.
PW-1 informant of the case has stated that no vehicle was recovered from the accused before him.
He did not see the accused while driving the vehicle.

Similarly, PW-2 Harish Kumar Yadav, who is the driver of the car, has also stated in his cross-examination, that no recovery of vehicle took place from the present accused and he did not see the accused while driving the vehicle.
8. From the evidence of both the witnesses, it is proved that neither any recovery was made before them nor did they see the accused while driving the vehicle.

In this matter, since the present accused-Manish is not named in the FIR and the victim of the case i.e. Harish Kumar Yadav has also stated in his examination in-chief that he could not identify the person who offered him prasad,
since he had worn a scarf.
The accused-Manish was summoned on the Court on warrant.
No recovery was made from him.
Even, there was no evidence on record that he had been named in any case in the past.

9. Thus, the learned trial court found that the prosecution utterly failed to prove its case against the respondent-accused beyond reasonable doubt and it accordingly recorded the findings of acquittal.
10. We are in full agreement with the findings recorded by the learned trial court for recording the acquittal of the respondents-accused.
No interference is warranted with the impugned judgment and order.
